subject:
Re: [LAZY CONSENSUS] Limiting number of opened pull requests for

messages.subject:
Re: [LAZY CONSENSUS] Limiting number of opened pull requests for
 users without write access
messages.body:
Respectfully, I disagree.

I think 5 open PRs is more than needed. I have been contributing to Airflow for a while and I do not think I ever had more than 5 open PRs at the same time. So I do not think having a cap of 5 PRs will you slow down in any way.

These days the bottleneck is clearly reviewing PRs and not creating PRs, so I do not think we should consider whether some contributors would like to have more than 5 open PRs, but whether the community has the capacity to review more than 5 PRs per contributor. I think the answer is no. I understand allowing more than 5 open PRs would be an an exception to the rule (we would only allow-list some contributors), still, I do not think we need that exception. I would not mind being capped to 5 open PR to be honest.

My 2 cents.

On 2026/09/21 18:34:59 Henry Chen wrote:
> I agree this could discourage contributors from contributing. As a middle ground, maybe we could maintain a "trust list" to exclude people we really trust from the limit which, as Damian pointed out, GitHub already supports natively. That might actually encourage contributors to review their PRs more carefully, since active contributors who want to do this right have an incentive to build up their reputation and earn a spot on that list.
> 
> 
> Thanks
> Henry

messages.body:
And to add here: I propose that this thread (and "LAZY CONSENSUS") - will
run until Thursday the 24th at 12:00 CEST.

Only a committer's "-1"  might break the consensus, but I would like the
discussion on the cap to last until Thursday, regardless if consensus is
broken.

And if it's broken, or if we cannot get to a consensus to a number - we
will follow up with regular vote.

J.
